clue.text: A pair point in distress at ghost

indicators.note: something in distress is in disorder, so the letters of these words are thrown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A couple point in alarm at a spectre they have just seen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in distress' rearranges the ten letters of A PAIR POINT.
explanation.definitionFit: An apparition is a spectral figure, a phantom seen as if real.

clue.text: Affectations of a tax-collector

parts.note: the IRS, the Internal Revenue Service, collects taxes in the United States

explanation.surface: The mannerisms of a taxman are being described.
explanation.walkthrough: The IRS is the US federal tax agency.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting on airs means showing pretentious mannerisms, so the plural noun matches affectations.

clue.text: Paint that's a swine for chaps to produce on time

parts.note: a swine is a pig
chaps are men

explanation.surface: A tricky paint job proves a real pain for the workmen to finish on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a swine' reads as slang for a nuisance, but it simply supplies the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A pigment is a colouring substance, the stuff a paint is made from.

clue.text: Reunion mater organised as a reward

indicators.note: something organised has been arranged, so the letters of these two words are set out afresh

explanation.surface: Mother arranges a family reunion as a treat for everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' rearranges the letters of REUNION MATER.
explanation.definitionFit: Remuneration is payment given for work or service, a recompense.

clue.text: In principle, people need somewhere to live

indicators.note: placed In front of the word for principle, it puts the people inside the principle

parts.note: a tenet is a principle or belief
people, as in mankind, can be men

explanation.surface: A homeless campaigner argues that people need a place to live, as a matter of principle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'need' is a link word. 'In principle' reads as 'theoretically', but 'In' is the container signal. A tenement is a large block of rented flats.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenement is an apartment building, a dwelling place for many households.

clue.text: Began to write in the dictionary

indicators.note: the word in tells us the writing tool goes inside the dictionary

parts.note: the OED is the Oxford English Dictionary
to pen is to write

explanation.surface: A lexicographer started writing entries for the dictionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'write in the dictionary' looks like one action; 'in' is the container signal. The OED is the Oxford English Dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: To have opened something is to have started it, as a meeting is opened.

clue.text: The French in charge are not clerical

parts.note: la is a French word for the

explanation.surface: The French people running things are secular rather than churchmen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are' is a link word; IC is the usual crossword shorthand for in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Laic means lay, belonging to the laity rather than the priesthood.

clue.text: Declared everything — for example, to journalist

parts.note: all means everything
ED, an editor, is the crossword journalist

explanation.surface: Someone told a reporter everything, giving examples.
explanation.walkthrough: ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist.
explanation.definitionFit: Alleged means asserted or claimed, usually without proof.

clue.text: Shot out when a cult taped broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast can mean scattered widely, so the letters of these words are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone fired off when a sect recorded a programme for transmission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges the letters of A CULT TAPED; 'when' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To be catapulted is to be hurled or launched forcibly, as from a sling.

clue.text: Controlled diet programme Edward's on

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after, so the nickname follows the programme

parts.note: a regimen is a prescribed course of diet and exercise
Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Edward is following a strict diet plan to control his eating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diet programme' looks like the definition with 'Controlled', but it supplies the wordplay; in an across clue 'on' means following.
explanation.definitionFit: Regimented means strictly organised and disciplined, kept under tight order.

clue.text: Mop up stain

definitions.meaning: to soak up liquid with absorbent paper
a spot or mark, like one of ink

explanation.definitionFit: Blotting paper soaks up ink, and an inky smudge left behind is itself a mark of that name.

clue.text: It may see you through!

parts.note: sounds like something that helps you get by, but read literally it is a look so sharp it seems to pass right through you

explanation.definitionFit: A piercing look is an intense stare that seems to penetrate the person it falls upon.

clue.text: Plant producing iron for the navy

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A factory plant is turning out iron for the naval fleet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' suggests a factory; RN is the Royal Navy, Britain's navy.
explanation.definitionFit: A fern is a flowerless green plant with feathery fronds.

clue.text: Having a rendezvous when assembly ended

parts.note: an assembly is a meeting
up can mean ended, as in time is up

explanation.surface: People are getting together now that the conference has finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is a link word; 'up' means over, as in 'your time is up'.
explanation.definitionFit: To rendezvous is to come together with someone at an arranged place.

clue.text: Little writing can be of great importance

definitions.text: Little writing can be of great importance

parts.words: Little writing can be of great importance
parts.note: tiny text in a contract that, though easily missed, may carry the conditions that matter most

explanation.definitionFit: Contract terms printed in tiny type often contain crucial restrictions a signer may overlook.

clue.text: Growing up like victor?

definitions.meaning: playfully, acting like the film star Victor Mature, whose surname looks like the verb

explanation.walkthrough: Victor Mature was a Hollywood actor; with a small v, 'victor' hides the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Developing into adulthood is ripening, and the surname of actor Victor Mature makes a playful second sense.

clue.text: Backward boy with broken rib first to arrive at wedding

indicators.note: first says the shuffled rib comes before the boy
something broken is smashed up, so the letters of rib are reshuffled
Backward tells us to read the word for boy from right to left

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A slow-witted lad with a fractured rib is first to turn up at the wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges the rib, 'Backward' turns the boy round, and 'first' puts the shuffled rib ahead of him. 'to arrive at' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridal describes things belonging to a marriage ceremony, as in a bridal march.

clue.text: Unguided when drawing, but with complete control

definitions.meaning: given full licence to act as one likes

explanation.definitionFit: Freehand sketching uses no instruments, and having a free hand means unrestricted authority.

clue.text: Supporter took in ambassador

parts.note: a leg supports a body or a table
to take in food is to eat, so took in is ate

explanation.surface: A backer took in the visiting envoy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'took in' suggests deceived or housed, but here it means swallowed.
explanation.definitionFit: A legate is an envoy, especially one representing the Pope.

clue.text: German had an inclination, one gathered

parts.note: to have leaned is to have tilted or inclined

explanation.surface: A German was keen on something, and one person collected it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' is a link word; 'inclination' suggests a wish but here means a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: To glean is to collect bit by bit, as leftover grain after a harvest.

clue.text: If I trace the letters out, that's trickery!

indicators.note: trace the letters out means set them in a fresh layout, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that copying the characters would be cheating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the letters out' rearranges IF I TRACE.
explanation.definitionFit: Artifice means cunning deception, clever schemes used to mislead.

clue.text: Native American getting to a state

parts.note: an American Indian is a Native American

explanation.surface: An indigenous American is travelling to a particular US state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiana is one of the fifty United States, in the Midwest.

clue.text: Smoothly, with added love for 18 but less energy

indicators.note: with added says the love letter is attached at the end
less means minus, so the energy letter is taken away

parts.note: 18 refers to the answer to 18 across, the ambassador
E is the symbol for energy in physics
love is zero in tennis, and zero looks like O

explanation.surface: An envoy is smoother with a touch of love but less vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less' removes E from LEGATE, leaving LEGAT; 'with added' attaches O. 'for' and 'but' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Legato is a musical direction meaning play in a smooth, connected way.

clue.text: Union of niece with pole could be epoch-making

indicators.note: a union joins things together, so the letters of these two words are mixed into one new word

explanation.surface: A wedding uniting a niece and a Polish man could be a historic event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union of' rearranges NIECE POLE; 'with' and 'could be' are links. The Pleiocene, more often spelt Pliocene, is a geological epoch.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pliocene was a geological period, one making up an epoch of the Tertiary era.

clue.text: Deities one can track back to first sumerians

indicators.note: back tells us to read the tracking animal from right to left

parts.note: a dog can track a scent

indicators.note: first means take only the opening letter of sumerians

explanation.surface: An archaeologist traces the gods back to the earliest Sumerians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns DOG into GOD; 'first' takes S from 'sumerians'. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Gods are divine beings, objects of worship.

clue.text: Employs us to go to el Salvador

parts.note: ES is the international code for El Salvador

explanation.surface: A firm hires people like us to work in El Salvador.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To use something is to put it into service, to make use of it.

clue.text: Initially Irish-owned north Atlantic island

indicators.note: Initially means take the opening letter of each of the next four words

explanation.surface: An island in the north Atlantic was originally owned by the Irish.
explanation.walkthrough: Iona is an island of the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland, where St Columba founded a monastery.
explanation.definitionFit: Iona is a small Hebridean isle off the coast of Mull.

clue.text: Boats that move on the double?

definitions.text: Boats that move on the double?

parts.words: Boats that move on the double?
parts.note: on the double seems to mean quickly, but these vessels travel on two hulls

explanation.definitionFit: A catamaran is a vessel with twin parallel hulls joined by a frame.

clue.text: Fluctuation in main water supply

parts.note: sounds like a variable flow from the water mains, but the main is the sea and its level rises and falls

explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is an old poetic word for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea rises and falls twice daily under the pull of the moon.

clue.text: Good old gongs wanted by athletes

parts.note: gongs is British slang for medals or decorations

explanation.surface: Fine old decorations are the prizes that sports competitors covet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gongs' is British slang for medals.
explanation.definitionFit: Olympic winners receive top-tier prizes, the highest award athletes strive for.
